answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because falcon only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, comet is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any harbor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
